prompt: A 5.0 m ladder leans against a vertical wall, making an angle of $70^{\circ}$ with the horizontal ground. Find how far up the wall it reaches.
markscheme:
$h=5\sin70^{\circ}$ **(M1)** $=4.70$ m **(A1)**

The wall height is opposite the $70^{\circ}$ angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse, so use sine.

$\dfrac{b}{\sin65^{\circ}}=\dfrac{12}{\sin40^{\circ}}$ **(M1)** $\Rightarrow b=16.9$ cm **(A1)**

Use the sine rule when you know a side and its opposite angle.

prompt:
**(a)** In triangle $PQR$, $p=7$, $q=9$ and $R=50^{\circ}$. Find $r$. **[2]**

**(b)** A triangle has sides 5 cm, 7 cm and 10 cm. Find its largest angle. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $r^{2}=49+81-2(7)(9)\cos50^{\circ}$ **(M1)** $\Rightarrow r=7.00$ **(A1)**

**(b)** The largest angle is opposite the longest side: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{25+49-100}{2(5)(7)}=-\dfrac{26}{70}$ **(M1)**, $\theta=112^{\circ}$ **(A1)**

A negative cosine signals an obtuse angle — the cosine rule handles this automatically, unlike the sine rule.

concept: Area of a triangle ½ab sin C
prompt:
**(a)** Find the area of a triangle with sides 8 cm and 11 cm and included angle $35^{\circ}$. **[1]**

**(b)** A different triangle has sides 8 cm and 11 cm and area $30\ \text{cm}^{2}$. Find the possible sizes of the included angle. **[3]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\tfrac12(8)(11)\sin35^{\circ}=25.2\ \text{cm}^{2}$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $\tfrac12(8)(11)\sin C=30\Rightarrow\sin C=\dfrac{60}{88}$ **(M1)**

$C=43.0^{\circ}$ **(A1)** or $C=180^{\circ}-43.0^{\circ}=137^{\circ}$ **(A1)**

Both are valid because $\sin C=\sin(180^{\circ}-C)$.
